mu_name_from: MuProtocol/Items.cs and the old client's MuWeapons.cs both name axe index 5 the Battle Axe against Item/Axe06.bmd.
why_this_one: The first two-handed thing in the project, and chosen so the difference is the only thing that changes: it is an axe like the Small Axe already built, allowed to the Knight like everything else here, and MuWeapons.cs records it as TwoHanded with WeaponStance.TwoHandSword. So the character keeps its body, its armour and its hand, and swaps one stance for another.

stats.note: The item's own row, which is what decides the damage, the swing rate and who is allowed to hold it. Copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, so the call it came from is written out beside it and the two can be read against each other in one glance.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Weapons.cs. The 0.75 table, not Season 6's - the two agree on this row and disagree on others, and 0.75 is the version this server is being built to.
stats.drop_level_note: The lowest monster that may leave this, and whether one ever does. Both are already in the call above and were being read past: the bool before the name is dropsFromMonsters and the int after it is the drop level. They are lifted out here because the loot pool is now the built catalogue gated by this number - see shared/Loot.cs. Arrows, bolts and scrolls are shop stock in the original and fall from nothing, which is what the flag says and why a spider cannot leave a quiver.
stats.width_note: width is carried because it is where OpenMU keeps two-handedness: `if (group < Bows && width == 2)` sets IsTwoHandedWeaponEquipped. It is not read as the two_handed flag above - that one is the client's, out of MuWeapons.cs - but the two must agree, and a row where they do not is a transcription error caught for free.
stats.height_note: Height is the sixth argument of the call above and was not carried across when this row was first transcribed - see width_note, which explains why width was. Both are needed now that the bag has a footprint: an item occupies a rectangle of the inventory grid rather than one cell, so a Small Axe is one across and three down, and drawing it in a single square is what made every weapon read as a thumbnail. See Satchel.Covered, which walks the rectangle.
stats.attack_speed_note: attack_speed is a stat and not a rate. OpenMU adds it whole to the character's AttackSpeed - `AttackSpeed += 1 * AttackSpeedByWeapon` in CharacterClassInitialization - and the client then spends that as `PlaySpeed = base + AttackSpeed * 0.004` on the attack action. So a weapon makes its own animation run faster, and the swing rate follows from the animation. The Kris at 50 is more than twice the Small Axe at 20 and it is visible in the arm.
stats.skill_note: The skillNumber of the call. There are no skills in this simulation, so it is carried for the row to read against the call it came from and nothing more - and it is the reason this item is dearer in the original than the price MU2 charges, since OpenMU multiplies a skilled item's price by two and a half. See shared/Market's remarks.

stance_from: MuWeapons.cs: WeaponStance.TwoHandSword, TwoHanded: true. MuStances.For maps that to PLAYER_STOP_TWO_HAND_SWORD and PLAYER_WALK_TWO_HAND_SWORD, actions 5 and 18 - and TwoHanded is why the left hand has to be empty, because a shield goes in the hand a one-handed weapon leaves free and this one leaves none.
sheet_from: Data/Item/Axes07.OZJ (64x64), from MuMain. The .bmd names Axes07.jpg.
sheet_note: find_source turned up remaster_one's at exactly 2x, which is the shape it warns about by name. MuMain's is the art.
two_handed_from: MuWeapons.cs records TwoHanded: true beside the stance. It is a separate fact from the stance and not derivable from it - a wand is a stance of its own and one-handed, a bow is a stance of its own and is not - so it is declared rather than inferred.
material_note:
The same three-island shape the Small Axe has, and read the same way: crop each island at its own mu_uv with V flipped. It does not come out the same, though - a two-handed haft is a longer thing with more on it, so where the Small Axe went steel/steel/wood this goes plate/blade/wrap.

Island 2 was leather_wrap and is wood. This file's own note says 'where the Small Axe went steel/steel/wood this goes plate/blade/wrap', and the wrap is the half of that which does not survive measurement: the island's twelve triangles mean (100, 34, 16) at chroma 84 - red-brown, the colour of the banded haft strip in the top right of Axes07 - against the head's chroma 6 and 12. A two-handed axe does have a longer haft with more on it, which is what the note was reaching for, but longer is not a reason for it to stop being timber. leather_wrap's weave along u is also the banding fault that struck the quiver and the Morning Star in the same batch.
open_question: The head is one material where the art has two surfaces in it - a near-black cast body and a polished edge. Materials are assigned per UV island and the island covers both, so blade steel is the answer for the whole of it. Splitting them would want the assignment to be finer than an island.

islands.note: the shaft: a long dark length between the head and the grip, drawn the same blue-black as the head, so metal rather than timber. Forged rather than ground, though - it is a pole, not an edge - and at blade steel's 0.32 it came out a rod of black chrome with a highlight running down it. Plate's 0.68 is the same metal finished the way a shaft is finished.

the head. Thirty of the fifty-four triangles, sampling the whole sheet, and the one place on this weapon a ground edge actually lives - the same call the Small Axe's head got, and for the same reason.

the grip: the warm red strip along the top of the sheet, and the reason it is not the wood the Small Axe's haft was. It is banded - regular dark bars across its width, not streaks along its length - which is a cord wound round in turns, and that is what leather_wrap was made from and describes. Wood's grain would also have run the wrong way over it, lengthwise across the binding.
